items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: and Walter Page, was in the band.

ctx.x: Now the Southern Serenaders, at that time, they had in the band Hot Lips Page, who is from Corsicana, Texas, and later moved to Dallas. I've known him practically all of my life. Hot Lips Page at that time was playing like everything Louis Armstrong ever put out, note for note. If you put one in one room and one in another you could hardly tell them apart. What a great trumpet player!

They had another saxophone player, who I grew up with, named Bill Owens, and he was playing sax and clarinet, and Walter Page, was in the band. Jimmy Rushing was the singer. And by the way, Jimmy Rushing, the only thing saved us is Jimmy Rushing's people always owned a restaurant in Oklahoma City, and he made it possible for us to eat over there, and his parents' restaurant.

And so we had to get back to Dallas, so these guys were so kind. They had a man named Simpson that played trumpet; beautiful, beautiful trumpet player. And incidentally, this is at the time that I met Charlie Christian, who was a youngster, on the guitar, and he had heard Eddie Durham and when Eddie Durham was great and he had sort of copied some of his style, plus his own ability to --
